name: message_search_labeled_eval
description: Labeled ranking eval for GlobalDb::search_session_messages over a seeded synthetic corpus. Each query pins per-case ordering constraints (top-1, top-k membership sets, scoping exclusions) plus p@1/p@3/MRR metrics recomputed by the test from the LIVE ranking. Cases that current master ranks worse than the ranking we want are marked expected_current_failure:true: the test asserts the DOCUMENTED current outcome (so the suite is green now) while printing the aspirational one, forming a known-gap ledger the ranking fix must consciously flip.

metrics._comment: Mean p@1/p@3/MRR over the 10 positive queries, recomputed by the test from the LIVE ranking. mean_p_at_1 and mean_mrr are 1.0 because every positive query now ranks its sole relevant message first — including exact_branch_impl_over_inventory, where the shared application session compatibility classifier moves the branch-roster noise (inv-1/inv-2/inv-3) below the real implementation message impl-1. mean_p_at_3 stays 0.37: nine single-relevant queries contribute 1/3 each and multi_term_partial_coverage_order contributes 2/3, so (9*(1/3)+2/3)/10 = 0.3667 rounds to 0.37.

queries.label: exact_branch_impl_over_inventory
queries.note: Exact-branch query. The implementation session ranks above the branch-inventory noise: the shared application session compatibility classifier demotes the branch-roster messages (inv-1/inv-2/inv-3) that merely name-drop the branch below impl-1, the session that actually implemented it. Before the fix, bm25 alone put the short, dense inv-3 roster on top.

queries.label: relevance_beats_recency
queries.note: An older, richly-relevant decision message must outrank newer marginal mentions of the same rare term. bm25 is relevance-ranked with no recency term, so the old message wins on coverage.

queries.label: provider_filter_codex_scopes
queries.note: A shared term across three providers, scoped to codex, must return only the codex hit.

queries.label: provider_filter_cursor_scopes
queries.note: Same shared term scoped to cursor returns only the cursor hit.

queries.label: assistant_text_beats_tool_noise
queries.note: A focused assistant message must outrank a long, noisy tool_result that only mentions the term once, thanks to bm25 length normalization on the heavily-weighted text column.

queries.label: multi_term_full_coverage_top1
queries.note: A message covering all three query terms outranks partial-coverage messages.

queries.label: multi_term_partial_coverage_order
queries.note: Both multi-term messages must sit above the single-term message; the two-term relevant pair fills the top two ranks.

queries.label: case_insensitive_prefix_match
queries.note: An upper-case query term matches lower-case body text (FTS is case-insensitive).

queries.label: unique_rare_term_single_hit
queries.note: A term appearing in exactly one message returns exactly that message.

queries.label: project_scope_excludes_other_project
queries.note: The project_key filter must keep an identically-worded message from another project out of the results.

queries.label: negative_absent_term_empty
queries.note: A query whose only term appears nowhere returns no hits.

queries.label: negative_hyphen_literal_filter_empty
queries.note: The hyphenated term forces an exact-substring filter; with a matching plain term present, the hyphen literal still removes every row because no message contains it verbatim.
